canonical.stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy to supply the directions that were omitted from a written prescription already on file. A certified pharmacy technician takes the call after identifying herself as a certified pharmacy technician. What does the regulation permit?

Apply the current hazardous-drug handling requirements that govern the hazardous ingredient and compounding process.
Treat hazardous-drug status as replacing all other compounding requirements.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy licensed for sterile compounding prepares two products on the same morning: a sterile infusion for an outpatient, and a sterile preparation for a patient admitted as an inpatient in the same hospital under its institutional licence. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both containers must be labelled as a sterile compounded preparation.
The outpatient container must also carry the pharmacist-contact telephone number.
The telephone must be staffed during regular hours of operation and at least 56 hours a week.
The inpatient preparation must also carry the telephone number, since the pharmacy does sterile compounding.
The pharmacist reachable on that number must have access to the patient's records.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 sets two distinct duties. All drug preparations compounded by a board-licensed pharmacy must carry a label notifying users and practitioners that the drug is a sterile or non-sterile compounded preparation. Separately, pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding must provide a telephone number fostering communication between patients and a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records, staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week, affixed to the container alongside the compounded-preparation label. That telephone paragraph does not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed under c. 112, s. 39I where the sterile preparation is to be administered to an inpatient within the same hospital.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the compounded-preparation label duty reaches all such preparations.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the outpatient container falls squarely within the telephone paragraph.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: staffed during regular hours every day and not less than 56 hours per week.
choice_analysis.D: The telephone paragraph is disapplied for an inpatient preparation within the same hospital.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the pharmacist reached must have access to the patient's records.

related_facts: The carve-out is tied to administration within the same hospital, not merely to inpatient status
explanation.mpje_trap: One exception is written into one of the two paragraphs. Reading it as an exception to both strips the required compounded-preparation label from the inpatient container.

It has compounded a batch of sterile preparations and wants to ship them to a hospital in the Commonwealth while it waits for the inspection. May it?

choices.text: Yes, because the provisional registration authorises it to operate as a facility.
Yes, because the shipment stays inside the Commonwealth.
Yes, provided the receiving hospital records the provisional status.
No, because a provisional holder is barred from compounding until inspected.
No, because a provisional holder is permitted to compound but not to supply.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 21.03(3) provides that an entity with a provisional outsourcing facility registration MAY COMPOUND sterile drug preparations but MAY NOT DISTRIBUTE OR DISPENSE a sterile drug preparation within or outside the Commonwealth until it has been inspected by the FDA and has received a Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration. The permission and the prohibition sit in the same sentence.

choice_analysis.A: The registration authorises production, not supply.
choice_analysis.B: The prohibition covers supply within and outside the Commonwealth alike.
choice_analysis.C: No recording by the recipient cures the prohibition.
choice_analysis.D: Compounding is expressly permitted.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: compounding yes, distribution or dispensing no.

related_facts: A non-resident outsourcing facility cannot hold a provisional registration at all
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a registration that permits production as permitting supply of what is produced.

public.stem:
Case A: A Massachusetts resident outsourcing facility has provisional status under a pathway allowing preparation while the required FDA inspection and full approval remain outstanding.

Case B: A nonresident outsourcing supplier presents its federal registration listing as the only evidence that it may supply Massachusetts.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The provisional preparation pathway does not itself authorize distribution or dispensing before the required inspection and full approval.
The nonresident supplier must establish applicable Massachusetts approval and relevant home-state and inspection conditions.
State renewal timing and federal annual registration may require separate calendars.
A relocation must follow the applicable advance application and new-location approval requirements.

explanation.core_reasoning: Provisional에서 허용된 preparation과 full authority가 필요한 출고를 구분한다. FDA 공개 등록명부의 존재와 MA에서 공급할 자격은 같지 않다. 연방·주의 서로 다른 갱신 체계를 한 번의 제출로 처리하지 않는다. 사업장 주소 변경과 검사·승인·신청 시점을 별도로 관리한다.

choice_analysis.B: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. FDA 공개 등록명부의 존재와 MA에서 공급할 자격은 같지 않다.

canonical.stem: A less expensive drug product is reasonably available and appears on the Massachusetts interchangeable-drug list, but the prescription contains a valid prescriber no-substitution direction. Which statements correctly describe the product-selection decision? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The valid no-substitution direction prevents the pharmacist from applying the usual required interchange on this prescription.
A lower price does not override a valid prescriber no-substitution direction.

Without a valid no-substitution direction, the Massachusetts interchange framework generally requires use of the reasonably available, less expensive interchangeable product when its conditions are met.
The patient may erase the prescriber's valid no-substitution direction and compel interchange without prescriber involvement.
Before interchanging, the pharmacist must still confirm that the alternative satisfies the Massachusetts interchangeable-product framework rather than relying on price alone.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts product selection depends on interchange eligibility, price/availability conditions, and the prescriber's substitution direction. A valid no-substitution instruction controls despite a lower price and blocks the otherwise applicable interchange rule. When substitution is permitted, the pharmacist still must use a legally interchangeable product rather than treating lower price alone as sufficient.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. A valid prescriber no-substitution direction is a controlling exception to interchange.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. Lower price does not nullify a valid no-substitution instruction.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. In the absence of a valid no-substitution instruction, the statutory interchange conditions apply.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The patient cannot simply erase the prescriber's valid direction and convert it into a substitution-authorized prescription.
choice_analysis.E: Correct. Price is not enough by itself; the selected alternative must satisfy the governing interchangeable-product requirements.

related_facts: Product-selection law belongs to the NABP Area-4 practice-operations competency rather than prescription-transfer/dispensing mechanics.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not let price or inventory status override a valid prescriber no-substitution direction.

public.stem:
Case A: A sponsor has an investigational new drug pathway for clinical research and describes it to a retail pharmacy as approval to market the product for routine patient prescriptions.

Case B: A different product has an approved ANDA, and staff assume this permits substituting it for products with other routes and release formulations without a product-specific interchange assessment.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A BLA is the individual dispensing pharmacist's professional license.
An IND-related research pathway is not the same as marketing approval for routine retail sale.
ANDA approval establishes pharmacist substitution across all routes and release formulations of the ingredient.
Submitting an NDA establishes that the proposed drug is approved for marketing.

explanation.core_reasoning: 연구용 사용·운송 경로와 일반 판매승인을 분리한다. 제품 승인과 정확한 제형·route·strength·TE·주법상 대체조제 판단은 다르다. BLA·NDA·ANDA·IND가 답하는 규제 질문을 구별한다. 신청 접수·심사·승인 상태를 같은 것으로 처리하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. BLA·NDA·ANDA·IND가 답하는 규제 질문을 구별한다.
교정된 설명: A BLA is the licensing application pathway for biological products, rather than a pharmacy's professional license.
choice_analysis.B: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. 연구용 사용·운송 경로와 일반 판매승인을 분리한다.
choice_analysis.C:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 제품 승인과 정확한 제형·route·strength·TE·주법상 대체조제 판단은 다르다.
교정된 설명: The ANDA approval does not establish interchangeability across unrelated routes or release formulations.
choice_analysis.D:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 신청 접수·심사·승인 상태를 같은 것으로 처리하지 않는다.
교정된 설명: Submission of an NDA and approval of that application are different regulatory states.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing staff for the Board-approved pharmacy technician assessment examination. Which knowledge areas does the regulation require the examination to cover? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Laws and regulations regarding the practice of pharmacy and patient confidentiality.
The duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician in relationship to other pharmacy personnel.
Sterile compounding gowning procedures and aseptic technique.
Medical abbreviations and symbols.
Identification of drugs, dosages, routes of administration and storage requirements.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.02(5) lists the knowledge areas a Board-approved examination shall cover: practice settings; the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician in relationship to other pharmacy personnel; laws and regulations regarding the practice of pharmacy and patient confidentiality; medical abbreviations and symbols; common dosage calculations; and identification of drugs, dosages, routes of administration and storage requirements. Sterile compounding technique is not among them.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: law and confidentiality is a named area.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: relationship to other pharmacy personnel is a named area.
choice_analysis.C: Sterile compounding technique is not among the listed examination areas.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: medical abbreviations and symbols is a named area.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: drug, dosage, route and storage identification is a named area.

related_facts: Practice settings and common dosage calculations are the two remaining listed areas.
explanation.mpje_trap: The list is specific, so a plausible pharmacy topic can still fall outside the prescribed examination areas.
